description: An open source AI wearable device that captures what you say and hear in the real world and then transcribes and stores it on your own server. You can then chat with Adeus using the app, and it will have all the right context about what you want to talk about - a truly personalized, personal AI.

summary.one_liner: Adeus is an open-source AI wearable concept that records what the user says and hears, transcribes it, stores it on the user's own server, and lets them chat with a personal AI that draws on that context.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes three parts: a mobile/web app for chatting with a personal AI and viewing data, a wearable hardware device that records what the user says or hears and sends it to the backend, and a Supabase backend that processes and stores data and interacts with LLMs. The stated goal is that the AI has context about the user's recorded conversations so responses are personalized. The README says data is stored on the user's own server. It notes that active development has moved to a separate "Friend" repo and a Discord community. The README is short and gives no setup instructions or detailed feature list.
use_cases: Record and transcribe real-world conversations with a wearable
Build a personal AI that remembers context from your day
Keep personal audio transcripts on a self-hosted server
Chat with an AI that knows your recorded conversations
Experiment with open-source wearable AI hardware
how_to_run: Refer to the Getting Started Guide linked in the README (no commands are given in the README itself)
notable: Wearable hardware device that captures speech from the real world
Stores transcripts on the user's own server, with data ownership emphasized
Chat interface gives a personal AI access to recorded context
Backend built on Supabase, which handles LLM interaction
caveats: README says active development has moved to the separate Friend repo and Discord community, so this repo may be out of date
README gives no install or run instructions beyond a link to the Getting Started Guide
License is listed as NOASSERTION on GitHub and not named in the README
